effects.log: You leave the ground before the first footstep. Let {him} hunt an empty valley.

ok.log: You knew every move before {he} made it. {npc} goes down, and does not understand how.

fail.log: Knowing was not enough. You get away, bleeding, with the old dread back in you.

events.text: Poachers have come up from the valley with nets and long knives, after the young of your ground. They have not seen you yet.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: They run, and leave their nets behind them in the ferns.

fail.log: They drive you off with fire and clubs, and take what they came for.

choices.text: Let them take what they came for, this once

effects.log: You watch them go down the mountain with their sacks. It sits badly in you for a year.

events.text: Another of your kind, younger and hungrier, has come into your ground and means to keep it. It does not bow.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: It goes back the way it came, slower than it arrived.

fail.log: It takes the best of your ground from you, for now.

choices.text: Give it the far edge and keep the heart

effects.log: You give up the far edge. It is enough for it, for a while.

events.text: A pack of wild dogs, starving after the hard winter, has found you and decided you are food.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The pack scatters into the snow, and does not come back.

fail.log: They harry you for three days before they give up.

choices.text: Go up where they cannot climb

effects.log: You go up the rocks and wait. They howl at you all night, and are gone by morning.

events.text: Boys from the village have dared each other up the slope to throw stones at the thing that lives there. One of them is good with a sling.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: They flee shrieking, and that night every child in the village is told the story.

fail.log: A stone finds you, and the boys run home heroes.

choices.text: Let them see you, once, and nothing more

effects.log: You lift your head from the shadow and look at them. They go down the slope much faster than they came up.

events.text: A trapper has strung the gully with iron jaws. One of them has nearly closed on you already. The trapper is coming to check the line.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: You break the line and the trapper runs, leaving the iron to rust.

fail.log: The trapper drives you off and keeps the line strung.

choices.text: Spring every trap with a stick and go

effects.log: You spend a night springing every jaw on the line. The trapper finds them all empty and shut, and does not come back.

events.text: A great boar, scarred and mad with age, has rooted up your feeding ground and stands in the middle of it, daring anything to move it.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The boar goes, grunting, into the oaks.

fail.log: The boar keeps the ground, and you nurse your hurts.

choices.text: Wait for it to move on

effects.log: It takes a season. You go hungry the while.

events.text: Men with spears and torches are beating the hills for you: the county has sent soldiers. They mean to kill you, and they have the numbers to try.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The line breaks and the soldiers run down the hill, dropping torches.

fail.log: There are too many of them. You get away, burnt and hurt.

choices.text: Go so deep they lose the trail

effects.log: You go where no road goes. The soldiers burn an empty hillside and march home.

events.text: An exorcist has come with a bell, a sword of peachwood and a long paper of names, and is chanting yours. The air tightens around you. This is a rite to destroy you.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The bell cracks, the paper burns, and the exorcist goes down the mountain without them.

fail.log: The rite holds. You tear free of it, but not whole.

choices.text: Leave the ground until the rite is spent

effects.log: You go far away until the chanting stops. The exorcist declares the mountain clean, and is paid.

events.text: A cultivator of the martial world has come to take your core for an elixir. They have a sword that hums and they are very sure of themselves.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The sword stops humming. Its owner leaves without it.

fail.log: You lose the fight, and some of your strength with it, but not your core.

choices.text: Show them one breath of what you are, and wait

effects.log: You let them feel it for one breath. They decide your core is not worth their life, and go.

events.text: A bandit camp has moved into the valley under your ground, and has started taking the villages' rice. The villagers have left offerings at your stones, asking.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The bandits leave the valley the same night, all of them, and the rice goes back.

fail.log: The bandits beat you off with fire. The villages go on paying.

choices.text: Leave it to the humans

effects.log: You do nothing. The offerings at your stones stop coming.

events.text: Something old and ill-tempered has come down from the high peaks to take your ground: a beast as great as you, and older.

choices.text: Fight

roll.foeName: The great beast of the peaks

ok.log: It goes back up to the snow with its pride hurt, and leaves you the valley.

fail.log: It takes the valley. You keep your life and your lower slopes.

choices.text: Yield the high ground to it

effects.log: You give it the high ground. It is enough for it.

events.text: The spear corps of a great house have tracked you for a month. They have nets of braided iron and an order to bring back your head. A hunt to the death.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The nets tear, the line breaks, and the spear corps carries its wounded home.

fail.log: You break out of the iron net, torn and bleeding.

choices.text: Draw them into the river and vanish

effects.log: You go into the river and let it carry you a day downstream. The corps hunts the bank for a month.

events.text: An army is camped on the plain below you, waiting for the pass to clear, and their general has been told what lives above the pass. The archers are already climbing.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The archers come back down without their bows, and the army goes the long way round.

fail.log: Too many arrows. You get above them with your hide full of shafts.

choices.text: Close the pass with weather and let them wait

effects.log: You bring the cloud down on the pass. The army waits a month and goes home.

variants: Campfires on the plain below, hundreds of them, and an army waiting for the pass. Someone has told their general what sleeps above it. At first light the archers start up the slope in a long grey line.

The army on the plain has stopped waiting for the snow to clear. Their general wants the pass, and wants what lives above it gone first. You hear the archers before you see them: boots on scree, a sergeant counting.
Banners in the valley, and a general who has heard the stories and does not believe them. The archers are sent up the mountain to prove the stories wrong.

events.text: Three masters of the martial world have sworn to bring your hide back to their hall, and have come together. They are very good, and they are not afraid.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: One after another the three masters go down, and the one who can still walk carries the other two home.

fail.log: They wound you badly and lose their nerve before they can finish it.

choices.text: Speak to them in their own tongue

effects.log: You speak, and the three masters go pale, and bow, and leave.

events.text: A beast that heaven itself has sent, white and burning, has come down on the storm to measure you. It does not speak. It only waits for you to rise.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: It goes back up into the storm. Heaven has measured you, and found you enough.

fail.log: It throws you down and leaves. Heaven has measured you, and found you wanting, for now.

choices.text: Bow to it and do not rise

effects.log: You bow your head to the ground. It looks at you a long time and goes back up into the cloud.

events.text: A sorcerer of the old kind has dug a pit of runes under your sleeping place and is calling you into it, to bind you to a jar. The pull is very strong.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The runes crack. The jar shatters. The sorcerer runs, and never digs a pit again.

fail.log: You tear out of the binding half-bound, and it takes years to shake it off.

choices.text: Sleep through it, deep enough that it cannot find you

effects.log: You go down into the deepest sleep you have. The sorcerer calls into an empty pit for a month.

variants: You wake heavy. While you slept, a sorcerer of the old kind cut a ring of runes into the stone around you, and the ring is pulling, slow and strong, toward the mouth of a clay jar.
There is chanting under the ground where you sleep. An old-style sorcerer has buried a ring of runes beneath you, and every word of the chant drags you a little nearer to the jar brought for you.
A smell of burnt hair and cinnabar: a sorcerer has been at work while you slept, and the runes in the earth under you are already awake. The sorcerer wants you in a jar, sealed, on a shelf.

events.text: Another great beast of your strength, whose range touches yours, has decided the line between you is in the wrong place.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The line is where you say it is now, and every lesser beast on both sides knows it.

fail.log: The line moves your way. You lose a valley.

choices.text: Meet it at the line and talk

effects.log: It takes a whole season of growling. The line stays where it was.

events.text: Grave-robbers have broken into the old tomb in your ground, the one you have kept for a hundred years for a king nobody remembers.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: The robbers flee and the tomb is sealed again, by you.

fail.log: They get away with the king's cup and two of his jars.

choices.text: Let them take one thing, and frighten them off the rest

effects.log: They run with one cup. The rest stays where the king left it.

variants: Torches in the old tomb again. Grave-robbers have dug through the side of the mound you have watched over for a hundred years, for a king whose name the rain washed off the stone long ago.
Someone has found the old tomb in your ground: a broken seal, a shovel left by the door, and voices inside, arguing over a king's grave goods. You have kept that king's sleep a hundred years.

The forgotten king's mound has a hole in it this morning, and fresh earth beside it. Grave-robbers, down in the dark among the jars and the bronze, taking what you have guarded since before their grandfathers were born.

events.text: After the worst of it you open your eyes and the night is not dark. Every living thing in your ground glows faint as the moon on water, and the ones who mean you harm glow cold.

effects.log: You let it come. It is yours now.

effects.log: It does not pass. It waits for you behind the lid, patient as stone.

events.text: The old ones of the mountains speak of a spring on the moon road where the moon lies in the water all night. A grey eye washed in it, they say, sees again. You have found it.

choices.text: Wash the grey eye in the moon

effects.log: The water is so cold it burns.

choices.text: Not yet. You fear what it will show you

effects.log: You leave the spring alone. It will be there.

events.text: A white crane has stood on the rock above your sleeping place for three nights. On the fourth it drops a single drop of something silver in front of you and flies off. It smells of moonlight.

choices.text: Take it into the grey eye

effects.log: It stings, and then it does not.

choices.text: Leave it on the rock

effects.log: The silver drop dries in the sun by noon.

events.text: A traveller sits down by the shrine at the foot of your mountain and tells the story of you to a crowd of strangers. At the end of it they have a name for you, and they say it like a prayer.

effects.log: You let them have it. It is not your name, but it is the one they will remember.

choices.text: Turn your back on it

events.text: The pool, the cold, the slow fish: all of it as it was. But you remember a thousand years of it already, and how it ended. This time you know where the pearl will fall.

events.text: It is out. Someone saw you at the water's edge in your true shape, and by noon the whole town knows. They are gathering in the square with torches, and they are afraid.

choices.text: Flee, and leave the whole life behind

effects.log: You go, and do not look back.

choices.text: Show yourself as you are, and ask to stay

ok.log: There is a long silence, and then an old woman steps forward and bows.

fail.log: They cannot bear to look at you. You go.
